entities.summary: Sabinus of Piacenza was a Christian bishop who played a significant role in the development of Christianity in Northern Italy during the late Roman Empire. Born into a noble family, Sabinus rose through the ranks to become Bishop of Piacenza around 400 CE and continued to serve until his death in 421 CE. His tenure was marked by controversy over the use of baptismal fonts, which he opposed due to concerns about the purity of water. This stance led to a rift with the imperial authorities and the Christian community. Despite this, Sabinus remained committed to his faith and worked tirelessly to promote the teachings of Christianity throughout the region.
